moves.rejection_reason: precedent-supported but verifier confidence 0.85 is below 0.92

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, CBP held origin was China because only an unmachined stainless steel card blank was produced in Vietnam before being sent to China. In Variant B, all machining, heat treatment, sharpening, black oxide finishing, and laser etching of the stainless steel card are performed in Vietnam, leaving only simple assembly of the finished card with a polyester rope in China. Under N334762 and N350962, the formed and machined stainless steel tool body imparts the essential character of a multi-tool, and simple assembly with a cord in China does not substantially transform the Vietnamese tool.

moves.description: Make Machining, heat treatment and finishing and Handles and hardware in Vietnam
moves.rejection_reason: precedent-supported but verifier confidence 0.75 is below 0.92

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, only the unmachined stainless steel card blank was made in Vietnam, while the rope and remaining processing occurred in China. In Variant B, ALL components (the SUS420 stainless steel card and the polyester rope) are produced in Vietnam, where the steel card also undergoes machining, heat treatment, sharpening, black oxide finishing, and laser etching. Only minimal final assembly (attaching the finished card and polyester cord together) remains in China. Under National Hand Tool Corp. and general CBP substantial transformation doctrine (cited in N351687 and N352429), merely attaching a cord in China does not substantially transform completely fabricated Vietnamese components.

moves.description: Make Handles and hardware in Vietnam
moves.rejection_reason: no earlier ruling found where CBP held this kind of change decisive

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, CBP held origin is China (N354220) despite the SUS420 stainless steel card blank being produced in Vietnam, implying that the finishing/machining of the blank in China (or the Chinese processing) conferred origin. In Variant B, the only change is shifting the production of the auxiliary polyester rope/handle element from China to Vietnam, while the card blank and final assembly remain split the same way. Under N334762 and N350962, shifting secondary handle/grip components does not alter the country of origin of a multi-tool, which is governed by where the steel working tool receives its essential character.
